meiji_transition.summary: In 1871 Ōtsu and Nagahama prefectures were created, merging as Shiga in 1872; from 1876 to 1881 Wakasa and Echizen's Tsuruga District were briefly part of Shiga.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Shiga = Ōmi Province. 'Ōmi' means the freshwater lake near the capital (Lake Biwa), as opposed to 'Tōtōmi' (Lake Hamana).

history_timeline.title: Ōmi Ōtsu Palace
history_timeline.summary: Emperor Tenji moved the capital to Ōmi Ōtsu Palace in 667; Saichō founded Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei in 788.

history_timeline.title: The Sasaki of Ōmi
history_timeline.summary: The Uda Genji Sasaki held the governorship of Ōmi; from them came the Rokkaku and Kyōgoku houses.

history_timeline.title: Rokkaku and Kyōgoku
history_timeline.summary: The Rokkaku governed southern Ōmi, the Kyōgoku the north; Sasaki Dōyo of the Kyōgoku was a famous 'basara' lord of the Northern and Southern Courts era.

history_timeline.title: Azuchi Castle
history_timeline.summary: Azai Nagamasa held Odani Castle (Battle of Anegawa, 1570); in 1576 Nobunaga built Azuchi Castle, whose keep set the model for early-modern castles, burned after the Honnō-ji Incident in 1582.

history_timeline.title: Ōmi merchants
history_timeline.summary: The Ii of Hikone led the fudai lords, and the great elder Ii Naosuke signed the commercial treaties; Ōmi merchants, devoted to 'sanpō yoshi' (good for seller, buyer and society), spread across Japan.

history_timeline.title: The Lake Biwa Canal
history_timeline.summary: The 1890 Lake Biwa Canal brought water and hydropower to Kyoto; Lake Biwa supplies about 14.5 million people in Kinki.

landmarks.name: Shirahige Shrine
landmarks.note: A torii standing in Lake Biwa

specialties.name: Ōmi beef
specialties.note: One of Japan's three great wagyu

dialect.name: Ōmi dialect
dialect.features: A Kansai dialect with '-haru' and '-hen' endings, more direct than Kyoto speech; 'hokasu' means to throw away.

guide.opening: I once followed Emperor Tenji's carriage to the Ōmi Ōtsu Palace, and I still remember the shimmer of Lake Biwa. Lord Nobunaga's Azuchi Castle stood by the lake too — which tale would you hear?

regional_meme.title: Kansai water wars
regional_meme.text: A Shiga person's trump card in any argument: 'Keep it up and we'll shut the Lake Biwa sluice gates — no water for Kyoto and Osaka!'

regional_meme.title: Lake Biwa's size
regional_meme.text: Lake Biwa covers about a sixth of Shiga; locals give directions by 'which side of the lake'.

hero_persona.name: Ishida Mitsunari
hero_persona.title: Commander of the Western Army · a man of righteousness
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Ishida Jibu-no-shō Mitsunari, of Ōmi. They say no one liked me — but all I wanted was to protect the late Taikō's realm.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: earnest and rigid, principled and socially awkward, but unwavering in loyalty to the Toyotomi

ramen.toppings: Cabbage, bean sprouts, pork, wood-ear mushrooms
ramen.highlight: Clear golden dashi with heaps of vegetables — add vinegar to change the taste

sake.taste_profile: Rich & dry: named for the Seven Spears of Shizugatake, mellower with age
